end.summary:
• 30 + 70 = 100 was shown, including a tens explanation.
• Partners for 2-digit numbers were practised; 65 + 35 and 48 + 52 were given correctly, with some mixed answers.
• The 65 + 45 error was corrected later in the lesson.
• Number-line jumps from 48 to 50 and from 50 to 100 were practised; the final route used 5, then four jumps of 10.
end.parentNote: Asha practised making 100 with tens numbers and with two-digit numbers, using place-value explanations and number-line jumps. Vihaan showed the tens method with 30 + 70 and later corrected the 65 + 45 mix-up; two-digit partners still need more checking next time. At home, ask them to find partners for 48, 65, and two other two-digit numbers, then check each sum by adding it to 100.
